originalTitle: Is this $450 laptop from an unknown brand too good to be true?

content: Finding a good laptop under $500 was hard enough before RAMageddon. They nearly always had cheap hardware and underpowered, often outdated chips. That’s what made the MacBook Neo so disruptive: It offered great build quality and good-enough performance starting at $599. Windows laptops couldn’t touch it. Even though it’s gone up to $699, it’s still the laptop to beat. So when little-known Chinese brand Chuwi announced a $450 Windows laptop with an aluminum build and a brand-new Intel Wildcat Lake processor, it sounded too good to be true. It is. [Product: Chuwi UniBook | https://us.chuwi.com/products/unibook-laptop-intel-core-3-304-series-3-wildcat-lake] The UniBook comes in one configuration: a 14-inch with an Intel Core 3 304 processor, 8GB of soldered RAM, and a user-swappable 256GB SSD. That’s the lowest-end of Intel’s new Wildcat Lake chips, with just five CPU cores: one performance core, and four low-power efficiency cores. And the integrated graphics? A single GPU core. The MacBook Neo’s A18 Pro is a six-core CPU / five-core GPU ensemble, and it’s a hot rod by comparison. --- Component report card * Screen: D * Webcam: D * Keyboard: C * Trackpad: F * Port selection: A * Speakers: F * Number of ugly stickers to remove: 1 --- The UniBook feels sluggish in anything beyond basic web browsing, emails, and messaging. Its benchmark scores confirm how woefully underpowered that chip is. The MacBook Neo trounces it across the board: both single and multicore CPU performance, as well as graphics. Our Adobe Premiere 4K export test took over an hour on the UniBook. (Although at least it didn’t crash out.) I know it isn’t designed for video editing, but neither is the MacBook Neo, and the Neo exports the same video in under 10 minutes. The one edge the UniBook has is a slightly faster SSD. But despite faster storage, the UniBook’s 8GB of RAM is still a hindrance on Windows 11. It didn’t randomly lag like the recent 13-inch Surface Laptop did, but it isn’t hard to overwhelm. As on the 8GB Surface, Windows 11 uses anywhere from 4.6 to over 5GB of memory on the UniBook after a fresh reboot with no additional apps running. Once you open a half dozen Chrome tabs, a couple messaging apps, and a music streaming app, memory usage easily climbs to 7GB.  It’s no surprise Chrome crashed on me a couple times when I pushed it further with over 20 tabs across multiple virtual desktops. This is no problem on Windows laptops with 16GB of RAM, and even the MacBook Neo could handle more before slowing down. And you can count on everything moving like molasses during big file transfers. It couldn’t even load the Start menu or open the calculator app while importing photos into Lightroom Classic until the RAM and SSD bottlenecks eased.  [Image: Simple looks. Frustrating use. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/268691_Chuwi_UniBook_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0011.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Even if your computing needs are minimal, the Chuwi’s hardware makes every interaction unpleasant. The screen is washed out, covering just 64 percent of the sRGB color space, and at 300 nits it’s pretty dim. But the worst offender is the trackpad. It’s incredibly stiff to click. You have to press it so hard the whole chassis flexes a little under the pressure. You don’t have to click the trackpad; it can detect taps too, but I never like the loosey-goosey feel of tapping — especially when executing right-clicks or click-and-drags. Using this trackpad made me physically and mentally tired. And clicking around on a laptop? Pretty important! The speakers are an affront to any music you play, as well as anyone else within earshot. They’re a tinny mess. The phone in your pocket has fuller sound. The 720p webcam is only a smidge better, but it’s still offensive to your face (and possibly your self-confidence). It’s almost passable in the best lighting, but it’s low-res, with a green color cast. In dim or backlit lighting you become a dark blur. After a few days, colleagues started greeting me in meetings with, “Oh, you must be on the Chuwi.” It’s like being told “Wow, you look tired.” “Uhh, yeah. Nice to see you too.”  [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/268691_Chuwi_UniBook_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0006.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/268691_Chuwi_UniBook_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0007.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/268691_Chuwi_UniBook_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0002.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Amid all these downsides, there are a few bright spots. The UniBook does at least have good battery life. It easily lasts up to 10 hours on battery while doing the lightest of work: writing emails, casually browsing the web, and opening the occasional PDF. And the keyboard isn’t bad. It’s backlit, which is a genuine advantage over the MacBook Neo. It’s fine to type on, but the Neo’s and many other Windows keyboards out there feel less spongy. Also, a lack of function lock means adjusting brightness, volume, or media playback always requires a two-key combo. Not a huge deal, but a strange omission of a usual mainstay. The one thing about the UniBook that genuinely surprised me, aside from the initial reverse sticker shock, was its amount of ports. This little thing has five total USB ports, HDMI-out, microSD, and even an ethernet jack. You might expect all that on a massive gaming laptop, not a thin-and-light. But sadly, none of the USBs are faster than 5Gbps, and the HDMI is just 1.4b — topping out at a stuttery 30Hz at 4K. Any money spent on peripherals to offset the Chuwi’s shortcomings would be better spent on a different laptop. I’ve started testing a $500-ish HP OmniBook 3, and coming from the Chuwi, it was a huge relief. chineseContent: 在 RAMgeddon 出现之前，找到一台 500 美元以下的优质笔记本电脑已经够难的了。他们几乎总是拥有廉价的硬件和动力不足且常常过时的芯片。这就是 MacBook Neo 如此具有颠覆性的原因：它提供了出色的制造质量和足够好的性能，起价 599 美元。 Windows 笔记本电脑无法触及它。尽管价格涨至 699 美元，但它仍然是一款无与伦比的笔记本电脑。因此，当鲜为人知的中国品牌驰为 (Chuwi) 宣布推出一款售价 450 美元、采用铝制结构和全新英特尔 Wildcat Lake 处理器的 Windows 笔记本电脑时，这听起来好得令人难以置信。这是。 [产品：驰为UniBook | https://us.chuwi.com/products/unibook-laptop-intel-core-3-304-series-3-wildcat-lake] UniBook 有一种配置：14 英寸，配备 Intel Core 3 304 处理器、8GB 焊接 RAM 和用户可插拔的 256GB SSD。这是英特尔全新 Wildcat Lake 芯片的最低端，只有五个 CPU 核心：一个性能核心和四个低功耗效率核心。那么集成显卡呢？单个 GPU 核心。 MacBook Neo 的 A18 Pro 是六核 CPU/五核 GPU 组合，相比之下它是一款热棒。 --- 组件报告卡 * 屏幕：D * 网络摄像头：D * 键盘：C * 触控板：F * 端口选择：A * 扬声器：F * 要移除的丑陋贴纸数量：1 --- 除了基本的网页浏览、电子邮件和消息传递之外，UniBook 在任何方面都感觉迟缓。它的基准测试分数证实了该芯片的性能严重不足。 MacBook Neo 在单核和多核 CPU 性能以及图形方面全面击败了它。我们的 Adob​​e Premiere 4K 导出测试在 UniBook 上花费了一个多小时。 （虽然至少它没有崩溃。）我知道它不是为视频编辑而设计的，但 MacBook Neo 也不是，Neo 在 10 分钟内导出相同的视频。 UniBook 的一个优势是轻微的
